321.t: Inventing a piano part and strumming for Thad
321.s: Thad grunted approval when Danko played bell tones and strummed, becoming his signature unlike Hanna or McNeely.
321.q: Yeah. And sometimes it’ll go, like it’ll be a two staff thing with all the voicings written out, which is nice. But then it will go to some single staff with some slashes in it you know. So it’s like really, it’s one of those things where it comes down to your ears listening to it and then seeing…

321.t: First Monday with the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band
321.s: After a quartet gig with Thad, Mel gave him the charts in advance; he describes what Mel's drumming meant to the band.
321.q: looking for somebody for the band.” You know and I was like, and I truthfully didn’t know a whole lot about the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band. I knew Thad as a player. I knew his Five by Five, the Monk records that he did and also what he did early on with Mingus, “The Jazz Experiments of Charles…

464.t: Forming the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band: studio players and Monday rehearsals
464.s: The band was created for Thad's writing, drawing studio players and young musicians, rehearsing Monday midnights at Jim and Andy's and then at A&R with Phil Ramone. The rehearsal tapes are lost.
464.q: Basically that’s what it was. It wasn’t formed for that reason, it was formed to have Thad write some music. And he used some of the best players in New York, who most of them were great jazz musicians, but who were very busy in the studios. Snooky Young on trumpet, Jerome Richardson on saxophone,…

464.t: The Village Vanguard Monday nights and leaving the band for Herbie Mann
464.s: The Vanguard offer drew packed houses and let Max Gordon open all week. Owens left after about three months because Mel Lewis would not let him take time off for the Herbie Mann tour, so he is not on the first records.
464.q: won’t pay a lot of money, maybe $20 a man, but I want to know if you want to go into the Village Vanguard on Monday nights.” And everybody said yeah. So he told Max Gordon, yeah, okay, we’ll go into the Village Vanguard. And at that particular time, this is 1965, 66, clubs in New York were really…

678.t: Subbing for Pepper Adams in the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band
678.s: He subbed for Pepper Adams for two and a half or three years and recorded Central Park North; Thad's melodic writing.
678.ch: Woody Herman, Buddy Rich and Thad Jones
678.q: Well that came about when I used to sub sometimes for Pepper. And around, I think it was around ‘68, somewhere around there, ‘68 or ‘69, Pepper’s mother got very sick. And he decided that he wanted to go back to Detroit to take care of her, which I thought was a wonderful thing for anyone, and…

678.t: Monday nights at the Vanguard and the band's roster
678.s: Visitors at the Vanguard, being overawed by the stars in the band, and the saxophone section.
678.ch: Woody Herman, Buddy Rich and Thad Jones
678.q: At the Vanguard. Every Monday. And you used to see — all kinds of people used to come in there: Don Byas, Ray Nance, Paul Gonzalves, a whole lot of people used to come in on Monday nights. It used to be a wonderful experience.

367.t: Founding member of the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band
367.s: Young joined the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band while on the Tonight Show, calls it the best band he played in, and remembers Thad as a close friend and roommate.
367.q: That band you‘re talking about. Let‘s see who formed that band? I played in the first band when they first started because me and Thad was like that coming out of Basie‘s band. We were like brothers. So when he and Mel Lewis formed that band I was playing the Tonight Show and they asked me would I…

367.t: Origins of the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band
367.s: Studio musicians in New York wanted to play, so Thad and Mel formed a band that rehearsed anytime and played Mondays at the Village Vanguard.
367.q: Well that band came about, there were a bunch of musicians in New York that was all mostly doing studio work. And so Thad and Mel come up with the idea. I don’t know exactly who came up with the idea, Conners, a guy names Conners, oh, I forget his name. He lives in — anyway, they got this idea of…

931.t: How he joined the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band and Thad's gifts
931.s: Knowing Thad and Mel separately, Dodgion accepted Mel's call and describes the band as his best musical experience, praising Thad as soloist, writer and conductor.
931.q: Gee. I knew Thad, I had met him in San Francisco when he was with Count Basie, and we played together at an after hours place there. And I met Mel through playing with Peggy Lee in New York and then eventually with Benny Goodman. We went to Russia and Mel was the drummer with Benny Goodman. And I…

616.t: Thad Jones-Mel Lewis Orchestra and Toshiko
616.s: He subbed with Toshiko and played about a year with Thad Jones-Mel Lewis alongside Phil Woods, and praises Thad as leader.
616.q: Yes I did. I used to be one of the regular subs that played with her band. Oh there’s so many people I’ve played with. I can’t really think of them. Of course I played for almost a year with the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis orchestra, which was wonderful. I wish I’d played better at the time. I mean I was…

330.t: Helping Thad Jones form his band and the stolen tune
330.s: Hanna knew Thad from Detroit, gave him the idea for a band in Japan, played the Monday set, and Thad arranged his improvised tune.
330.ch: Composing and the Thad Jones band
330.q: When Thad left the Basie band in 1962 we were neighbors living in the same town. I had known Thad since the 40s from Detroit, Pontiac days you know. Thad lived in Pontiac, I lived in Detroit. And when he left the Basie band he got a gig at Columbia at CBS. His brother Hank was the pianist for…

337.t: Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band and the Vanguard
337.s: The hardest music he played, good pay and buses, Mel Lewis's album 'Aerial View', and the Monday Vanguard band.
337.q: I liked it very much. They were good people. It was the hardest music I ever played in my life because if you think it’s going here it’s not, it’s going to go here and there. And you can’t have a drink when you’re playing with that band because it’s hard, really hard music, harder than Maynard’s.…

932.t: Joining Woody Herman as lead trumpet; Thad Jones and Mel Lewis
932.s: Shear took the Woody Herman lead chair as a rite of passage; he also played in Mel Lewis's band while Thad Jones had left for Europe.
932.ch: Joan Rivers Show and Woody Herman
932.q: Yeah, that happened early on when I moved to Los Angeles, so I didn’t really — although I did do some studio work right away in L.A. I turned it down when they first called me. I’ll never forget it. It was in the evening and I had to play a gig. So during the gig I was saying I should take that…

933.t: Playing guitar on Thad Jones-Mel Lewis's Consummation
933.s: A closet jazzer who attended Village Vanguard Mondays, he was invited by Thad Jones to play on 'Consummation', including 'Ahunk Ahunk'.
933.ch: Saturday Night Live and Thad Jones
933.q: Well I used to go, on Monday nights I’d go down, because I was always loving big band stuff. And I would call myself, as far as jazz, I’d call myself a closet jazzer. ‘Cause I practice jazz at home and I used to listen to Wes Montgomery records and you know, Joe Pass, and all that stuff. And I…

934.t: Subbing in the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band
934.s: Joe Farrell sent him to sub in Thad and Mel's band; Thad stopped the band during his tenor solo.
934.q: end of a period in a sense that you follow the lead alto player. The music was a guide. When it was sax soli, when the saxes were playing, it’s like an improvised solo. I mean a sax soli, it’s almost like someone would play a solo and it’s orchestrated for five saxes or whatever. and the lead alto…

823.t: Thad Jones and Bob Rosengarden's Dick Cavett band
823.s: He recalls Thad Jones's care and criticism, the intimidating band, and the blowing rehearsals on Rosengarden's Cavett band.
823.q: He was wonderful. I was devastated when he left New York number one, and number two when I heard he was sick. I didn’t know what to do about it. He wasn’t taking any calls or anything. But I found out. Jerome Richardson told me what a special feeling Thad had for me, and I mean he brought me to…

328.t: Thad Jones, Mel Lewis and the Vanguard band
328.s: Hampton admired Thad Jones's writing; he wrote one chart for vocalist Bertie Green, and discusses Mel Lewis.
328.q: I used to go down and listen to them all the time, because, for all of us that are arrangers, Thad Jones is a phenomenon. The way he writes music is impossible. You don’t even try to learn to write music like that. You try to learn to write music as many ways as you can, but you don’t try to learn…

614.t: The Thad Jones - Mel Lewis band as a 'Bed and Board Band'
614.s: Herman says the Thad and Mel band was a Monday night band that took engagements just to have a band and fell apart outside New York.
614.ch: Looking back, big bands and sidemen
614.q: Well, I don't know if it was ever really organized. So that's really being candid, because for several years it was a Monday night band in New York City. Every Monday night they met and played the music. And then in more recent times, they've gone to different parts of the world, and tried to -- I…

70.s: Thad Jones asked him back to tenor trombone to play plunger; Jackson praises Jones's humorous writing and conducting but dislikes touring.
70.ch: After the road: New York, the profession and advice
70.q: Well, you know, Thad and I was in Basie's band together. And Thad, he didn't really know -- because I started playing bass trombone, you see, and by me playing bass trombone everybody thought that I had quit playing tenor altogether, you see.
